items.text: Several of its members cosponsored from its introduction a bill ending citizenship at birth for children born in the country unless a parent is a citizen, a permanent resident, or serving in the armed forces with legal status. An independent estimate for a similar measure put the births affected at about 255,000 a year, about 0.07 percent of the population.

Its board wrote to the head of government urging that immigration enforcement continue in a city where it had met protests, using every tool including emergency powers to deploy troops, that local governments limiting cooperation with it lose national funding, and that the department in charge of immigration enforcement be fully funded.

While funding for the department in charge of immigration enforcement had lapsed, rejected its own party leaders' plan and called for a party-only budget bill funding the whole department, with robust funding for immigration enforcement and border agencies, through the end of the head of government's term.

Pressed its party's leaders for a floor vote on a bill writing the head of government's border measures into law, including finishing the border wall, ending the release of migrants awaiting hearings, and tightening asylum standards.
